jobs.reference_role: Robe-free stage03 full body: identity, face, material palette and game-sprite rendering; armor coverage is redesigned for this rank.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE complete original Technomancien cybernetic player sprite for a 64×64 roguelike cell, full figure about58 native pixels high.
Input image is the approved WORKING DIRECTION of a robe-free machine priest: use its FACE, compact bare head, original ash-steel and charcoal materials, calm frontal stance and simple matte rendering as identity reference. Redesign only the amount and shape of protective shells for the requested stage. Do NOT simply copy the same armor coverage.
The character is nearly entirely robotic, an upright slender adult machine engineer with a compact smooth gunmetal cranium, same dark mechanical face, restrained bronze lower jaw and ONE amber optic on viewer left. No flesh. Normal small head, short neck nested in the shoulder structure. Keep head proportions and identity across the range. Two distinct empty mechanical humanoid hands slightly away from torso, articulated elbows and hips, two separate feet fully visible. Mechanical limbs and pelvis exposed or armored to the requested stage.
Absolutely NO robe, hood, cowl, cape, tabard, apron, skirt, cloth, coat, fabric sleeves, hanging panels, pouches, backpack, tentacles or extra arms. No priest insignia, religious emblems, skulls, chains, ornament, staff, tool, weapon, halo, glowing chest or effects. Do not introduce a second optic. No giant head or long neck.
Class identity: visible robotic chassis and rounded/tapered steel shells, a slender vertical torso with a compact pelvis, clear dark articulations and negative spaces between limbs. NOT the Bastion's broad square shoulders, blocky brawler plates, barrel chest or massive human musculature. He becomes more protected as a robot, not dressed as a muscular soldier.
Materials: smoky charcoal inner chassis, broad pale ash STEEL protective shells with quiet grey shadow planes, small existing bronze jaw accents only. No red/gold robes or bright chest paint. Broad clean two- or three-value planes, economical structural shapes. No tiny cables, rivets, vents, ribbed hoses, dense bevels, microtexture, tiny luminous accents or decorative pixels. Native64 readability is the main goal.
Complete coherent full figure from crown to soles, subtle elevated almost-frontal game-sprite view as reference, unchanged neutral stance, gentle upper-left light, restrained dark silhouette edges. Genuine transparent background with empty margins, no ground or cast shadow. No text, numbers, sheet, portraits or close-up.
STAGE 1/5, VERY LIGHT. A mostly exposed slender robot CHASSIS: narrow gunmetal upper body with two broad readable structural rib-side planes and a tiny central pale steel sternum pad; small modest shoulder joint caps only, exposed dark tubular upper arms, narrow unarmored forearms and simple small pale hand backs. Bare mechanical hip frame, thighs and shins with ONLY a few small light protective knee and ankle blocks, narrow practical steel feet. Large dark chassis masses alternating with a few pale guard surfaces, not an intricate skeleton. At native scale about25 pixels wide, clearly less covered than the reference stage03. No full breastplate, solid shoulder shells, long forearm guards, closed thigh shells or broad calf greaves.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one complete Technomancien character sprite, NO ROBE study for a cyberpunk roguelike, intended for 58 pixels inside a 64×64 cell.
Input image 1 is the existing whole middle-tier Technomancien. Preserve its mechanical FACE identity, single small amber optic on viewer left, compact head size, short neck, frontal stance, two empty articulated hands slightly away from body, original steel forearm/upper-arm guards, boots and clean matte game-sprite rendering.
Primary request: REMOVE ALL ROBE, hood, cowl, cape, fabric mantle, tabard, apron, hanging cloth, skirt and long coat. Make the near-fully robotic humanoid body visible from a small bare mechanical cranium to feet. There is absolutely no fabric garment anywhere. This is an original cybernetic engineer with a sober machine-priest composure, expressed through his upright calm posture and nearly total mechanical replacement rather than religious dress.
Keep the original slim vertical cyborg proportions and original medium protection stage. Build the newly exposed torso around the existing narrow gunmetal sternum armor, with two broad simple steel rib-side shells, a small compact pelvis guard, clearly articulated hips and separate slim armored robotic thighs/knees/calves. The inner chassis and joints are deep charcoal gunmetal, the guards quiet lighter ash steel matching the original arms and boots. No broad brawler shoulders or large muscular chest. Leave readable dark gaps at shoulder, elbow, waist, hip and knee joints. Only a few large simple structural shapes, not ribbed microdetails.
HEAD: remove the cloth hood completely. Retain the exact original small mechanical face and amber optic, with a close smooth dark metal cranial shell following a normal small human head, no helmet crest, no giant dome, no tall crown. The neck is short and nested directly in the shoulder frame. Keep the restrained bronze jaw already on the reference. No added gold religious trim, no red robe or red hanging panels, no new ornament or icons.
Hard invariants: two arms, two hands, two legs, two feet; same overall adult scale, feet fully visible, no weapon or object; preserve normal compact head and hands; no extra mechanical arms, tentacles, trailing cables, backpack towers, staff, skulls, goggles, chest emblems, cross, ceremonial ornaments, glowing halos, spikes, smoke or effects. No beige cloth, belts with pouches, soldier uniform or medieval armor.
Style: clean coherent game sprite, subtle elevated almost frontal view as reference, large economical matte planes, 2–3 values per material, soft upper-left light, restrained edges, no tiny rivets, no detailed technical illustration, no thick black lines around every component. Native64 readability through the silhouette and contrast of dark joints against pale steel guards. Same transparent background and full-figure framing with generous margins, no ground or cast shadow, no text or logo.
Output ONE whole coherent character, not a sheet or close-up. This is a new robe-free body study; do not merely hide the hem and keep a caped upper half.
